classification_signals: Page 3: 'TABLE OF CONTENTS' outlines sections defining biophilia, its principles, and application, indicating a structured presentation of a concept.
Page 3: 'The Practice of Biophilic Design' is presented as a standalone article available on www.biophilic-design.com, suggesting a conceptual or white paper.
Page 4: Discusses the origin of biophilia and human evolution, citing foundational works (Wilson 1986, Kellert 1997, 2012).
Page 5: Refers to 'a growing body of scientific study' and 'a wide range of studies have reported' to support claims, indicating a review of existing evidence.
Page 7: Introduces 'certain basic principles' for biophilic design.
Page 10: Presents 'Three kinds of experience of nature' and '24 attributes of biophilic design' as a core framework.
Page 21: Discusses 'The Ecological and Ethical Imperative', framing biophilic design as a practical methodology and a new consciousness.
title: THE PRACTICE OF BIOPHILIC DESIGN
authors: Stephen R. Kellert, Elizabeth F. Calabrese

minimum_safe_summary: This paper presents a comprehensive conceptual framework for biophilic design, defining it as the practice of creating human habitats that satisfy our inherent inclination to affiliate with nature. It outlines five core principles and categorizes 24 specific attributes across direct, indirect, and spatial experiences of nature. The framework posits that successful biophilic design enhances physical, mental, and behavioral wellbeing, including reducing stress, improving cognitive performance, and fostering a sense of place and responsibility towards the natural world. The authors argue that biophilic design is not merely an aesthetic choice but an ecological and ethical imperative for human health and sustainable environments.

theory_commitments.specific_claim: Humans possess an innate tendency to connect with nature and other living systems, and this connection is fundamental for their physical and mental health and well-being.
Biophilic design principles can be applied in built environments to satisfy the innate human need for nature, thereby enhancing occupant health, productivity, and overall quality of life.
Exposure to natural elements or views of nature can facilitate mental restoration and improve cognitive function by reducing directed attention fatigue.
Interactions with natural environments or biophilic elements can reduce physiological stress indicators (e.g., heart rate, blood pressure) and promote positive emotional states.

mechanism_chain.description: Biophilic design elements provide sensory experiences of nature, which engage restorative psychological and physiological processes, leading to improved health and well-being.
